Rust ownership is the set of rules that determines who is responsible for a value, when that value can be accessed, and when its memory is released. The compiler enforces these rules at compile time, so Rust can provide memory safety without a garbage collector. Core rules Every value has one owner. When the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped. Ownership can be moved to another variable. A value can be borrowed with &T or &mut T, subject to Rust's borrowing rules. Example: Rust Copy fn main() { let first = String::from("hello"); let second = first; // ownership moves from first to second // println!("{}", first); // ERROR: first no longer owns the String println!("{}", second); } // second goes out of scope; String is dropped here
